findings.title: Missing key prop on <GrafanaRuleListItem> in mapped list
findings.body: In the `.map((ruleWithOrigin) => { ... })` body of FilterViewResults, the `case 'grafana'` branch renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> without a `key` prop, while the sibling branches (`case 'datasource'` and the default branch) set `key={key}`. Because the result is returned from inside a switch inside a `.map()` callback returning JSX, React requires a stable key on each top-level list item. Without it React will emit 'Each child in a list should have a unique key' warnings at runtime, and worse, the component instances/state for reordered/added/removed Grafana rules may be reused incorrectly, leading to stale UI (e.g. wrong rule metadata or stale expansion/popover state) when the filtered list changes. Fix: add `key={key}` to the <GrafanaRuleListItem> element so it matches the other branches.

findings.title: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated=false, regressing federated rule immutability
findings.body: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (line ~246) the federation check was changed from `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` to a hardcoded `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO. This hook is still used by `useRulerRuleAbility(s)` and therefore consumed outside the list view (e.g. RuleDetails/RuleViewer via RuleActionsButtons/AlertRuleMenu) where `rulerRule` IS defined. Federated rule groups (a Mimir feature) are supposed to be treated as immutable: their rules cannot be removed or edited by a tenant. With `isFederated=false`, federated rules now report Update/Delete abilities as supported and (depending on permissions) allowed, so the Delete menu item in AlertRuleMenu can render for federated Mimir rules and may cause DELETE requests that the API rejects. At minimum the rule is shown as editable/removable when it should not be, breaking existing RBAC guarantees of the rule details/viewer pages.

findings.title: canPause is computed via OR but Pause menu item is gated on rulerRule being defined
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu now computes `canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`, so for a Grafana rule in the new list view (where `rulerRule` is undefined) canPause is correctly driven by the GrafanaPromRule abilities. However the Pause <MenuItemPauseRule> is rendered behind the additional expression `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana'`, both of which are false when rulerRule is undefined. Result: the Pause menu item is never shown in the list view even though the ability system reports the user can pause. Either the render gate needs to be updated (e.g. use the grafana prom rule) or the gate should be removed if Pause cannot actually be performed from the list view; otherwise ability/capability state and UI will diverge.

findings.title: Brittle exact menu-item count assertion in menu visibility test
findings.body: The 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' test asserts `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` exactly. Because menu contents depend on abilities (Pause, Silence, Declare Incident, Duplicate, Copy link, Export, Delete, extension links, sub-menu children, dividers), any future addition of a menu item (e.g. re-enabling Pause without a ruler rule, declaring incident in dev, or restoring an extension link) will silently break the test or mask real regressions. Prefer asserting presence/absence of each expected item individually and omit the exact-count check, or factor the assertion via a helper that enumerates expected vs forbidden items.

findings.body: Line 289 contains `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate`. The trailing `// duplicate` does not document anything specific (it isn't a TODO, doesn't reference an issue, and isn't a useful annotation) and reads as dev noise. Remove or replace it with a meaningful comment to avoid future confusion.
